item.title: The Iran Endgame? Donald Trump’s Military Action Window
item.description: A limited military strike on the Iranian regime could go a long way to giving the Iranian people a chance to enact regime change on their own terms. The post The Iran Endgame? Donald Trump’s Military Action Window appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why Are Fighter Jet “Stand-Off Weapons” So Important?
item.description: “Stand-off” range is the range an aircraft must remain away from its target to avoid putting itself in danger—a vital consideration in modern air combat. The post Why Are Fighter Jet “Stand-Off Weapons” So Important? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why America Built Only One Plane Out of Titanium
item.description: Titanium is fantastically expensive, and difficult to fabricate, relative to other materials—meaning it was only ever practical to use on the world’s fastest plane. The post Why America Built Only One Plane Out of Titanium appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Department of Energy Ends ALARA
item.description: By ending the ALARA principle, DOE opens the door to science-based radiation regulation that could restore nuclear power’s competitiveness. item.title: Why the US Military Could Lose the Contest for Materials Crucial to AI
item.description: AI’s bottleneck is physical—competition for power, land, and metals risks sidelining US military needs as commercial AI outpaces national security planning. The rapidly rising energy demands of artificial intelligence (AI) compute are not a new problem. item.title: Why Do Fighter Jets Land So Much Faster than Commercial Aircraft?
item.description: In commercial aviation, landings are designed to be gentle, with the idea that travelers will avoid planes with rough landings—but military aircraft place far less emphasis on comfort. The post Why Do Fighter Jets Land So Much Faster than Commercial Aircraft? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why Trump Blinked on a Chinese Drone Ban
item.description: Trump’s decision not to ban Chinese drones from the United States is a clear sign that, at least for the time being, China has America over a barrel on trade. The post Why Trump Blinked on a Chinese Drone Ban appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: After Trump’s Military Wins, China Retreats into Space
item.description: The Chinese military’s “Project Nantianmen” is far from reality—but it shows that Beijing is thinking about the right questions for the future of space warfare. The post After Trump’s Military Wins, China Retreats into Space appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The US Army Is Getting (Some of) Its Horses Back
item.description: Two US Army Bases—Fort Riley in Kansas and Fort Hood in Texas—are expected to restore their "Military Working Equine" (MWE) programs in the coming annual budget. The post The US Army Is Getting (Some of) Its Horses Back appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: V2X Tempest Anti-Drone Buggies: The Last Line of Ukraine’s Air Defense?
item.description: The high cost of the drone buggy’s Hellfire missile—at around $200,000 per shot—means that it can only be used for emergency situations. The post V2X Tempest Anti-Drone Buggies: The Last Line of Ukraine’s Air Defense? appeared first on The National Interest.
